property_summary: After a Put call with any msg.value, the caller's balance in Acc must equal the msg.value sent, but the buggy contract leaves it at zero.
After a Put, the Acc[caller].balance must reflect the sent value; the buggy version leaves it unchanged, violating this invariant.
After any call to Put with msg.value > 0, the caller's balance in Acc must be exactly msg.value, but the buggy version leaves it at zero, violating this invariant for some input.
After a Put call where the balance before the call is 0, the balance after the call must be at least msg.value, but the buggy version leaves it at 0.
After any Put(...) call, the unlockTime of the sender must be the block.timestamp or the passed _unlockTime, whichever is greater. The bug sets it to 0, which is always less than block.timestamp.
After a Put call, for any sender, the unlockTime stored in Acc[sender] must be at least the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the bug sets it to 0, violating this invariant.

After a Put call, the unlockTime for the sender must be at least the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the bug sets it to 0, which is always less, so no time lock is enforced and Collect can succeed immediately.
After a Put call, there exists no Collect call with a non-zero amount that can succeed before block.timestamp reaches the provided unlock time, but the bug always allows immediate Collect.
For any Put call, the sender's unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp of that call; the bug sets it to 0, so a subsequent Collect can succeed before the intended unlock time.
After any sequence ending with Put, the acc.unlockTime of msg.sender must be >= block.timestamp; the bug leaves unlockTime unchanged, potentially staying below block.timestamp.

For any Put call, the caller's unlockTime is set to max(_unlockTime,block.timestamp); the mutant leaves it unchanged, so after Put with _unlockTime>current unlockTime the value stays below the new block.timestamp.

After a Put call, the caller's unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the mutant leaves unlockTime unchanged, so a Put with _unlockTime less than the previous unlockTime will not extend it, violating the invariant.

After any Put call, the caller's unlockTime strictly increases or stays at least block.timestamp; the mutant deletes the update so unlockTime never increases, breaking the invariant when _unlockTime is less than the current unlockTime.

After any Put call, the caller's unlockTime must be greater than or equal to the unlockTime before the call; the mutant never updates unlockTime, so a Put with _unlockTime greater than the current unlockTime fails to increase it.
For any caller, after Put, the unlockTime must be >= block.timestamp of the Put call; the mutant sets it to the current block.timestamp, violating this when the given _unlockTime is in the future.

After Put, the unlockTime recorded in the Acc mapping for the caller must equal the larger of block.timestamp and the supplied _unlockTime; the mutant always sets it to block.timestamp, so it violates this when _unlockTime is in the future.

After any Put, the caller's unlockTime must be >= the given _unlockTime argument; the mutant sets it to block.timestamp, so when _unlockTime is > block.timestamp the recorded unlockTime is strictly less than the given _unlockTime, violating the rule.

For any user, after a call to Put with a future unlockTime, calling Collect with a valid amount later should succeed before that future time on the mutant but fail on the reference (because the reference correctly sets unlockTime to the future, blocking early collection).

After a Put call, the caller's recorded unlockTime must equal the supplied _unlockTime if it is in the future, or block.timestamp otherwise; the mutant always sets it to block.timestamp, so for any future _unlockTime the recorded unlockTime is wrong.
A Collect that reduces balance below MinSum never succeeds after the unlock time has passed.
